bath_rift_acolyte: Hjalmar: Mavet pays me in cure. I've been cured eleven times this week.
bath_rift_acolyte_defeat: Hjalmar: Mavet's at the bottom. She's bottling the view.
bath_rift_acolyte_intro: Hjalmar: Breathe in. The first lungful is free.
bath_rift_sign: The acid has eaten the floor down to an older floor, and that one down to bone.

lines: Clear water drips from an etched spout. It tastes faintly of copper.
Your Spirlings drink and rest.
The mail boat to Quillmarch carries letters, crates and you. Only you are not on the manifest.
Mail Boatman: Quillmarch? Letters, crates and passengers. Passengers go under the crates.

burin_landing_customs_customs: Customs Clerk Britt: Declare your goods. Declare your name. We'll decide which one is real.
burin_landing_folk_1: Plank Reader Ebbe: I read the pier backwards every morning. Yesterday I found my father's name. He swore he never confessed.
burin_landing_folk_2: Crate Girl Mina: I unload the mail boat. Half the letters are love letters. The other half are the replies, forged.
burin_landing_folk_3: Old Harbourmaster Fenn: Wren Marlow came through here with a new face. Tipped me with the old one's money.

lines: Dock Nurse Agathe: Lie down. The planks are old plates, so don't read them. Some of the confessions are catching.

burin_landing_net_loft_netter: Net Mender Joa: I fish the old plates out of the harbour. They make good planks and bad evidence.
burin_landing_post_office_postmaster: Postmaster Arvo: Your letter? Opened, read, resealed. Standard service.
burin_landing_sign: Burin Landing. All arrivals are recorded. Some are corrected.
burin_landing_tavern_innkeeper: Innkeeper Rune: Sailors drink here and sign their names on the wall. Wren signed it three times, three names.

lines: Pier Clerk Hollis: Tonics, ink and stamps. The stamps are real. The ink is mostly real.
burin_landing_trader.action: shop strong_tonic max_tonic remedy cooling_gel wake_bell revival_leaf dash_brew guard_brew

dead_letter_office_sign_1: Shelf label: 'Returned to sender. Sender returned to sender.'
dead_letter_office_sign_2: Pigeonholes up to the ceiling. Every one holds a letter nobody collected. Several are addressed to you.
debtors_icehouse_sign_1: Notice: 'Pledges are kept at four below. Complaints are kept next to them.'
debtors_icehouse_sign_2: Rows of ice blocks, each with a tag. Some of the tags are waving. No. That is the draught.
drypoint_lane_courier: Liv: I carry the Guild's letters. I read them first. It's in my contract, the part they didn't read.
drypoint_lane_courier_defeat: Liv: Fine. It says you're late. You are.
drypoint_lane_courier_intro: Liv: One of the letters is about you. Want to fight for it?
drypoint_lane_scratcher: Arne: I scratch plates by hand, no acid. Slower, cleaner, and nobody can prove which hand.
drypoint_lane_scratcher_intro: Arne: Your face would make a good plate. Let me rough it up first.
errata_chapel_sign_1: Plaque: 'Here we correct the dead. The living may queue.'
errata_chapel_sign_2: A wall of trial prints. 'Loving husband' is struck out on most of them.
gravers_causeway_canalman: Bo: I dredge the canal for lost plates. I find more lost people. They pay worse.
gravers_causeway_canalman_intro: Bo: You'd sink nicely. Let's test it.
gravers_causeway_graver: Osk: The Guild sends me to check who walks the causeway. Then it sends someone else to check me.
gravers_causeway_graver_defeat: Osk: You're on it now. Top line.
gravers_causeway_graver_intro: Osk: You're not on my list. Let's fix that.
hoarfrost_moor_hoarwatch: Eskil: The frost writes on the stones out here too. Mostly it writes: turn back.
hoarfrost_moor_hoarwatch_defeat: Eskil: Go on, then. The stones will remember you.
hoarfrost_moor_hoarwatch_intro: Eskil: You didn't turn back. Now you get me.
hoarfrost_moor_sledger: Runa: I haul the frozen out of the moor every spring. Some of them owe the Guild money. They still do.
hoarfrost_moor_sledger_defeat: Runa: Not today. The sledge is disappointed.
hoarfrost_moor_sledger_intro: Runa: My sledge has room for one more.
ledger_rift_acolyte: Bertram: I keep Ottoline's third ledger. The one for the other two.
ledger_rift_acolyte_defeat: Bertram: Balanced. I'll unbalance it later.
ledger_rift_sign: Pages drift in the dark like snow. Each one is a debt, and each debt has two totals.

lines: Clear water drips from an etched spout. It tastes faintly of copper.
Your Spirlings drink and rest.

ledgerholm_archive_elder: Archivist Solveig: Every book in here has a twin. Nobody knows which twin is the liar.
ledgerholm_bank_banker: Banker Leopold: We keep the true ledger. The other bank keeps the other true ledger.
ledgerholm_choir_loft_singer: Choirmaster Edvin: Bankers and forgers sing together on Sundays. The harmony is suspicious.
ledgerholm_folk_1: Forger Ulla: I copy banknotes on weekdays and sing in the choir on Sundays. The bankers sing bass.
ledgerholm_folk_2: Junior Banker Kaspar: My job is to tell the two ledgers apart. I was hired because I can't.
ledgerholm_folk_3: Old Auditor Hedvig: I audited Ottoline once. She audited me back. Now I live here, on a pension I didn't earn.
ledgerholm_forgery_forger: Forger Agnete: I don't forge. I restore documents to what they should have said.

lines: Bank Nurse Rasmine: Rest, then sign here. And here. The second one says you rested.

ledgerholm_sign: Ledgerholm. Two banks, one street, no witnesses.

lines: Counting Clerk Mads: Tonics at today's rate. Tomorrow's rate is better, but you might not be here.
ledgerholm_trader.action: shop strong_tonic max_tonic remedy cooling_gel wake_bell revival_leaf dash_brew guard_brew

mordant_row_apothecary_elder: Apothecary Gerold: Mavet's cure, three coins a bottle. The bottle is worth two of them.
mordant_row_bath_house_attendant: Bath Attendant Wilma: Towel? It's acid-proof. You aren't.
mordant_row_folk_1: Vat Stirrer Klaas: Lost my eyebrows the first day, my sense of smell the second. Lost my wife on the third, but that was the cards.
mordant_row_folk_2: Cure Seller Ottla: Mavet's cure works wonders. You only need it because of Mavet. Don't say that loudly.
mordant_row_folk_3: Widow Grete: My husband fell in the big bath. They etched his name on the rim. Took four seconds.

lines: Bath Nurse Doro: Rest here. The fumes don't reach this bench. Mostly.

mordant_row_sign: Mordant Row. Breathe through cloth. Bring your own cloth.
mordant_row_vat_store_stirrer: Vat Keeper Ronja: Empty vats in the back, full vats in front. The middle ones are complicated.
mordant_row_well_house_keeper: Well Keeper Tamm: Don't drink from the well. Don't ask why. Definitely don't ask Mavet why.
mordant_steps_fumer: Tilla: I bottle the fumes for Mavet's cure. Then I take the cure. It's a closed loop.
mordant_steps_fumer_defeat: Tilla: You held your breath. Cheat.
mordant_steps_fumer_intro: Tilla: Take a deep breath. Go on.
mordant_steps_stepcounter: Gisli: Every step is etched with the name of someone who slipped. I'm running out of steps.
mordant_steps_stepcounter_intro: Gisli: There's a blank step just here. Shall we fill it?
platewick_folk_1: Apprentice Tovi: I engraved my master's portrait. The Guild printed it on a wanted poster. Now I'm the master.
platewick_folk_2: Model Sanne: I sit for portraits. I've been hanged in effigy six times. Pays better than modelling.
platewick_folk_3: Old Engraver Brom: Every face I ever cut is still in a drawer upstairs. Some of them still owe me.
platewick_guild_hall_elder: Guild Warden Henrike: The Guild protects its members. From each other, mostly.

lines: Engraver's Nurse Ilka: Sit still. I patch people the way I patch plates: nobody notices the scratch until it prints.

platewick_plate_store_keeper: Plate Keeper Ove: Ten thousand copper faces. One of them is yours already. Don't ask who ordered it.
platewick_print_shop_printer: Printer Lasse: We print news in the morning and corrections at night. The corrections sell better.
platewick_sign: Platewick. Portraits while you wait. Wanted posters while you run.
platewick_studio_artist: Portraitist Lisbet: Hold still. Smile. Don't smile, the Guild prefers the wanted posters grim.

lines: Burin Seller Pell: Tonics and tools. A sharp burin opens many doors. Some of them are locked for good reason.
platewick_trader.action: shop strong_tonic max_tonic remedy cooling_gel wake_bell revival_leaf dash_brew guard_brew

press_rift_acolyte: Ylva: Grisel prints the Rifts and then sends people to seal them. Steady work for everyone.
press_rift_acolyte_defeat: Ylva: Clean print. Grisel will hate it.
press_rift_acolyte_intro: Ylva: You're the last job on the run. Let's see if you print clean.
press_rift_sign: A press the size of a church prints the map of Quillmarch, one Rift at a time.

lines: Clear water drips from an etched spout. It tastes faintly of copper.
Your Spirlings drink and rest.

proofgate_folk_1: Stamp Boy Egil: I stamp everything that leaves. Letters, crates, coffins. The coffins get two stamps.
proofgate_folk_2: Proofreader Malin: I read every map before it prints. Grisel moves the Rifts after I sign off.
proofgate_folk_3: Old Pressman Torvald: The edge of the map is just past the last press. I went to look once. They printed me coming back.

lines: Press Nurse Valda: Rest. If you wake up stamped, that's routine. If you wake up printed, complain.

proofgate_last_inn_innkeeper: Innkeeper Dagny: Last bed before the edge of the map. Pay in advance. Nobody pays on the way back.
proofgate_map_vault_keeper: Map Keeper Halvard: Every map of Quillmarch, printed here. Every Rift on them, put there by hand.
proofgate_proof_room_reader: Proof Reader Elin: I mark the errors in red. Grisel prints them anyway and calls them features.
proofgate_stamp_hall_stamper: Chief Stamper Birger: Approved, denied, deceased. Three stamps. I use the third one most.

lines: Bottle Washer Ida: Everyone who takes Mavet's cure comes back for more. Sicker. I wash the bottles. I've started counting.
Bottle Washer Ida: Find out what goes into the cure. Quietly. I'd ask myself, but I like my eyebrows.
Filler Boy Aki: The cure? Three parts bath water, one part well water, one part label. The label is the expensive part.
Filler Boy Aki: The well water comes from the Well House. They say don't drink it. So we sell it.

q3_cure_proof_aki_after: Filler Boy Aki: I drink beer. Nobody has cured beer yet.

lines: You take Ida's crate. Inside: three real tonics and two hundred labels reading 'Ida's Cure. Now with less Mavet.'
q3_cure_proof_ida_cure.action: set_flag q3_cure_proof_paid; give_item strong_tonic 3; quest_stage q3_cure_proof 4

q3_cure_proof_ida_cure_after: Ida: I wash bottles again. Mavet raised my pay. She said she admires initiative, and moved the pipe.
q3_cure_proof_ida_cure_defeat: Ida: Spilled. Two hundred bottles of it.
Ida: Take the tonics. They are real ones. I keep them for myself, which tells you everything.
q3_cure_proof_ida_cure_intro: Ida: Open wide. The first dose is free. So is the last.

lines: Bottle Washer Ida: Pipe forty-one. Bath to well to bottle. That's the whole recipe? That's all of it?
Bottle Washer Ida: Good. I've rented a cellar and bought two hundred bottles. Ida's Cure, half the price, same pipe.
Bottle Washer Ida: Only one person knows the recipe besides me and Mavet. And Mavet is a Warden.
Pipe Fitter Vera: This pipe runs from the big bath into the town well. I fitted it. Mavet drew the plan and paid in cure.
Pipe Fitter Vera: The well makes them ill, and the cure is the well. Write the pipe number down if you want proof. Forty-one.

q3_cure_proof_vera_after: Pipe Fitter Vera: I bring my own water. From Rimeholt. In a locked flask.
q3_cure_proof_wait: Bottle Washer Ida: The fillers on the Mordant Steps bottle it. Then ask in the Well House what they bottle.

lines: Osvald: There's a letter here for you. Posted eleven years ago.
Osvald: Unclaimed mail is released by duel. It's an old rule. I wrote it last week.

q3_dead_letter_office_defeat: Osvald: Delivered. Finally. That ruins my record.
q3_dead_letter_office_done: Osvald: No more mail for you. I checked twice. I was hoping.

lines: Osvald: Sign here. In case you lose, it says where to forward you.

q3_dead_letter_office_later: Osvald: It'll keep. It has kept eleven years. The ink is getting impatient, though.

lines: Osvald: Your letter. It says: 'Do not go to Quillmarch.' Unsigned. There was a parcel with it.
Pia: Look at my papers. 'Deceased.' One wrong stamp, and I can't buy bread, rent a bed or be arrested. I tried.
Pia: Get it corrected for me. They won't talk to me in the Stamp Hall. Company policy on the dead.
Paper Clerk Asmund: Swap papers for a dead girl? Already done, this morning. She came in herself. Very lively for her condition.
Paper Clerk Asmund: She signed for a traveller's papers and left her old ones in their place. I'd check your satchel, if I were you. Which, on paper, she now is.

q3_dead_stamp_asmund_after: Paper Clerk Asmund: Identity is nine tenths paperwork. The other tenth we lose.

lines: You take your papers back from Pia, and her satchel. Inside: two revival leaves, of all things.
q3_dead_stamp_pia_you.action: set_flag q3_dead_stamp_paid; give_item revival_leaf 2; quest_stage q3_dead_stamp 4

q3_dead_stamp_pia_you_after: Pia: I'm deceased again. They gave me a job in the Stamp Hall. Experience counts.
q3_dead_stamp_pia_you_defeat: Pia: Keep my old papers too. Being dead is restful. No one writes.
q3_dead_stamp_pia_you_intro: Pia: Don't make a scene. Dead people don't.

lines: Pia: You checked your satchel. Yes. I stamped myself dead two years ago. Debts die with you. It's the one honest rule in Quillmarch.
Pia: But the dead can't leave through Proofgate. The living can. So I needed a living set, and someone too busy to notice.
Pia: You are deceased, I am you, and the gate shuts at dusk. Nothing personal. That is rather the point.
Stamp Girl Tove: 'Deceased' can't be undone. Policy. But papers can be swapped, if somebody living signs theirs over.
Stamp Girl Tove: Unclaimed papers of the living end up in the Dead Letter Office on Drypoint Lane. Ask there. Don't say I said.

q3_dead_stamp_tove_after: Stamp Girl Tove: Approved, denied, deceased. I dream in three colours.
q3_dead_stamp_wait: Pia: The Stamp Hall is in Proofgate. Ask for the chief stamper's girl. She does the real work.

lines: Stig: Everything in here is pawned. Boots, fathers, a brass band.
Stig: Beat me and pick one thing from the unclaimed shelf.

q3_debtors_icehouse_defeat: Stig: Unclaimed shelf, left side. Not the tuba. The tuba is reserved.
q3_debtors_icehouse_done: Stig: The tuba plays at night. Nobody is in it. I have looked.

lines: Stig: Mind the floor. That is also somebody.

q3_debtors_icehouse_later: Stig: Wise. Half of them in here touched something.
q3_debtors_icehouse_lose: Stig: Row five has space. Just saying.

lines: Stig: You picked the crate of tonics. Everyone does. One day somebody takes the tuba and I can sleep.

q3_drypoint_lane_puller: Embla: I pull the first print of every plate. If it's a wanted poster, I get a head start.
q3_drypoint_lane_puller_defeat: Embla: Smudged. My fault. Write that down, it's rare.
q3_drypoint_lane_puller_intro: Embla: Let's see how you look in reverse.

lines: Corrector Brand: Welcome to the Errata Chapel. We print corrected epitaphs. 'Beloved' becomes 'tolerated'. Families pay well for accuracy.
Corrector Brand: Trouble is, epitaphs are being corrected before the people die. Someone is ahead of me. Find out who gets the lists.
You take Brand's cash box. Inside: three revival leaves and a receipt for your plot. Paid in full, with a view of the canal.
q3_early_epitaph_brand_stone.action: set_flag q3_early_epitaph_paid; give_item revival_leaf 3; quest_stage q3_early_epitaph 4

q3_early_epitaph_brand_stone_after: Brand: I corrected your stone. It now reads 'still alive, regrettably'. No charge.
q3_early_epitaph_brand_stone_defeat: Brand: An erratum. In my own chapel.
Brand: Take the stone money. And the stone. It is good granite. You'll want it one day.
q3_early_epitaph_brand_stone_intro: Brand: Here lies a stranger. Asked too many questions. Please lie down, the wording is final.

lines: Typesetter Hanne: Advance epitaphs, yes. Forty a month. Ordered and paid by Corrector Brand. He gets a discount for bulk.
Typesetter Hanne: He sells the plots before the debt falls due. There is one on the bench now. No name yet. Just 'a stranger, asked too many questions'.

q3_early_epitaph_hanne_after: Typesetter Hanne: I set my own stone once, for practice. Brand sent me a bill.

lines: Archive Runner Pim: The death lists? They aren't death lists. They are loans falling due. Same people, mostly. Same week.
Archive Runner Pim: A copy goes to the Print Shop in Platewick every month. Somebody there sets the stones in advance.

q3_early_epitaph_pim_after: Archive Runner Pim: I'm on a list myself. Small loan. Small stone.

lines: Corrector Brand: You went to the Print Shop. So you know who is ahead of me. I am. I'm very punctual.
Corrector Brand: A plot sold early is a plot sold twice. And a stranger who dies on the Causeway needs no family discount.
Corrector Brand: Your stone is already cut. It would be a shame to correct it.

q3_early_epitaph_wait: Corrector Brand: Names and dates come out of the Ledger Archive in Ledgerholm. Start with the archive runner.

lines: Map Apprentice Ansa: Hollow Em is gone from the new map. A whole village. Forty people who can't get a stamp because they aren't anywhere.
Map Apprentice Ansa: Find out who scraped it off the plate. And where it really lies. For the map. Only for the map.
Map Apprentice Ansa: Six weeks in the marsh and no village. I found three boots and a tax rider. I'm still looking. I count things.
Map Apprentice Ansa: Hollow Em is back on the map. In red. I have a house now. The door sticks.

q3_erased_village_folke: Folke: Marsh, mud, eels. I'm putting in for the desk job.
q3_erased_village_folke_defeat: Folke: All right. I found nothing. I'll put it on the form: 'nothing, with violence'.
Folke: The apprentice sold me your route for a fifth. She sells everything by the fraction.
q3_erased_village_folke_intro: Folke: You walk like someone who knows where forty taxpayers are hiding.

lines: Map Apprentice Ansa: The tax rider is on the Smudge Marsh. He follows your boot prints. Yours are the clean ones.
Eel Fisher Gudrun: Hush. Yes, I'm from Hollow Em. No map, no tax. We haven't paid in six years. Best six years we ever had.
Eel Fisher Gudrun: It lies behind the third dead alder, past the sunk cart. Don't tell the girl from Proofgate. She counts things.

q3_erased_village_gudrun_after: Eel Fisher Gudrun: If anyone asks, I'm a rumour.
q3_erased_village_hakon: Evicted Eeler Hakon: Six years of back tax. They took the boats, the nets and the eels. They left us the map.
Evicted Eeler Hakon: We're on it in red. Somebody told. I hope they got a good price.
q3_erased_village_keep: Map Apprentice Ansa: Past the mill, left at the gallows? Odd. Fine. Here, an advance. If it's wrong, I want it back with interest.

lines: Map Apprentice Ansa: You found it? Wonderful. I mean, for the map.
Map Apprentice Ansa: Fine. I get a tenth of every back tax I find. Six years, forty people. That's a house. With a door.
Map Apprentice Ansa: A tax rider is out on the marsh following your tracks. He takes a third if he finds it first. Stop him, then tell me where it is.
Map Apprentice Ansa: The rider is gone? Then it's just us. Where is Hollow Em?
Map Apprentice Ansa: Tell me and you get your share. Or tell me something else, and I'll never know. Probably.

choices.action: set_flag q3_erased_village_paid; give_item max_tonic 4; quest_stage q3_erased_village 4
set_flag q3_erased_village_paid; give_item strong_tonic 2; quest_stage q3_erased_village 4

lines: Vault Boy Sten: Hollow Em? Scraped off by order. Here's the slip: 'At the request of the village. Paid in eels.'
Vault Boy Sten: They asked to vanish. One of them still fishes on the Smudge Marsh. Follow the smell.

q3_erased_village_sten_after: Vault Boy Sten: I scraped my school off once. It was still there on Monday.
q3_erased_village_trust: Map Apprentice Ansa: Third dead alder, sunk cart. Thank you. Here is your share. Don't look at it like that, it's legal.
q3_erased_village_ulf: Eel Fisher's Boy Ulf: Gran says thank you, and that you were never here. Have an eel.
q3_erased_village_wait: Map Apprentice Ansa: The old plates lie in the Map Vault. Look at the scrape marks.

lines: Runhild: I cut one line for every visitor. Beat me and you choose the words.
Runhild: Lose and I choose. I'm in a mood today.

q3_errata_chapel_defeat: Runhild: Your words, then. Short ones, please. Granite charges by the letter.
q3_errata_chapel_done: Runhild: 'Not yet.' I had to cut it on a very small stone. Optimism doesn't sell.

lines: Runhild: The chisel is sharp. Hold your name steady.

q3_errata_chapel_later: Runhild: Everyone gets a line in the end. I can wait. I mostly do.

lines: Runhild: You chose 'Not yet'. Good line. Here, the chapel gives these to people it can't use yet.
Debtor's Daughter Kari: The Guild froze our house for a debt my father paid. He went to fetch the receipt and never came back.
Debtor's Daughter Kari: Find the receipt. With it the house thaws. Without it I sleep in the Hearth Hall, in the far row.
Debtor's Daughter Kari: Father is home. He keeps the receipt in one hand and the pawn ticket in the other. We don't talk much.
Debtor's Daughter Kari: The house is thawed. Father is still in row four. Spring is late this year. It was late last year too.
Debtor's Daughter Kari: The bailiff is on Rimeglass Pass. He carries a hammer and a candle. Go.

q3_frozen_deed_halfdan: Old Halfdan: Cold? No. I was cold for a year. Now I'm only disappointed.
Old Halfdan: She pawned me for the house. I'd have done the same to her mother. Still.
q3_frozen_deed_keep: Debtor's Daughter Kari: You paid the stamp? Oh. Then he'll be home tonight. I had better hide the pawn ticket.

lines: Sledge Boy Odd: The old man with the receipt? I drove him. Not to the Debt Office. To the Debtors' Icehouse, up on Rimeglass Pass.
Sledge Boy Odd: His daughter paid the fare. One way.

q3_frozen_deed_odd_after: Sledge Boy Odd: I don't ask where people go. I ask if they need the sledge back.
q3_frozen_deed_ragnvald: Ragnvald: I only collect. The cold does the rest.
q3_frozen_deed_ragnvald_defeat: Ragnvald: Keep the block, then. He holds the paper so hard we'd have to break the fingers anyway.
Ragnvald: The daughter told us you were coming, by the way. She wanted someone to blame if the ice cracked.
q3_frozen_deed_ragnvald_intro: Ragnvald: Receipts melt. People melt. The debt stays. Step aside.

lines: Debtor's Daughter Kari: You saw him? Then you know. I pawned my father. He was the only thing in the house the Guild would take.
Debtor's Daughter Kari: The receipt in his hand clears the debt. I need the receipt out and him... I hadn't planned that far.
Debtor's Daughter Kari: The Guild's bailiff is on his way to break the block and burn the paper. Stop him on the pass. Please.
Debtor's Daughter Kari: The block is safe? Then there are two ways to do this.
Debtor's Daughter Kari: Leave him to me. I'll have the receipt cut out neatly and thaw him in spring. Or pay the thaw stamp yourself, now, and he walks home with it.

choices.action: set_flag q3_frozen_deed_paid; give_item revival_leaf 3; quest_stage q3_frozen_deed 4
set_flag q3_frozen_deed_paid; give_item revival_leaf 1; quest_stage q3_frozen_deed 4

q3_frozen_deed_tagger: Tag Writer Inga: Row four, block nine? Renewed for another year this morning. By the daughter. She paid in firewood.

lines: Ice Keeper Torsten: Row four, block nine. An old man, standing, holding a receipt. Very good condition.
Ice Keeper Torsten: Pledged by his daughter against the house debt. The receipt is real. It's just inside the ice, with him.

q3_frozen_deed_torsten_after: Ice Keeper Torsten: We don't thaw without a stamp. We don't stamp without a fee. It keeps things calm.
q3_frozen_deed_trust: Debtor's Daughter Kari: Thank you. Spring. I promise. Springs are short here, but I promise.
q3_frozen_deed_wait: Debtor's Daughter Kari: He took the sledge road over the Hoarfrost Moor. Ask the people who work it.
q3_gravers_causeway_toller: Sixten: The Causeway toll is one coin or one portrait. I keep the portraits. They are useful later.
q3_gravers_causeway_toller_defeat: Sixten: Go on through. I'll draw you from memory. Unkindly.
q3_gravers_causeway_toller_intro: Sixten: Coin, portrait or a beating. I have engraved all three.
q3_hoarfrost_moor_reader: Yrsa: The frost wrote 'run' on my sledge this morning. I assumed it meant you.
q3_hoarfrost_moor_reader_defeat: Yrsa: It said 'loser'. It meant me. The frost is rude.
q3_hoarfrost_moor_reader_intro: Yrsa: Hold still. There is something written on your back.
q3_mordant_steps_carrier: Bodil: Two buckets up, two buckets down. I have one good shoulder and one very clean one.
q3_mordant_steps_carrier_defeat: Bodil: Not a drop spilled. Losing is easy when you're careful.
q3_mordant_steps_carrier_intro: Bodil: Careful. If I spill, we both get shorter.
q3_rimeglass_pass_cutter: Halla: I cut blocks for the Icehouse. Big ones. They never say what for, and I never measure anyone.
q3_rimeglass_pass_cutter_defeat: Halla: Too lively to store. Shame.
q3_rimeglass_pass_cutter_intro: Halla: You're about a block and a half. Let me check.

lines: Teller Nils: My till is one coin short every night. One. If the count is wrong a third time, the bank hangs the teller. It's in the rules, under 'staff benefits'.
Teller Nils: Find the thief. Ask loudly. I want people to see someone asking.
Coin Carter Brynja: One coin a night, yes. Teller Nils brings it himself. I restamp it lighter and send it back as two.
Coin Carter Brynja: Last week he asked me to remember a stranger instead. Asking questions, near the till. He described you rather well.

q3_short_till_brynja_after: Coin Carter Brynja: Money doesn't disappear. It just changes whose fault it is.

lines: Choir Boy Jens: I sing treble and watch the tills. Nobody goes near Nils's till. Only Nils. And lately you.
Choir Boy Jens: The missing coins turn up in the carts on Stamp Road, restamped. Ask the carter.

q3_short_till_jens_after: Choir Boy Jens: Bankers sing flat. They say the note is correct and the choir is in arrears.

lines: You take Nils's till bag. Inside: three tonics, forty light coins and a ledger page with your description. The height is flattering.
q3_short_till_nils_till.action: set_flag q3_short_till_paid; give_item max_tonic 3; quest_stage q3_short_till 4

q3_short_till_nils_till_after: Nils: I was promoted. The bank said a man who can frame a stranger can run the loans desk.
q3_short_till_nils_till_defeat: Nils: That doesn't add up. I checked it twice.
Nils: Take the coins. All the light ones. Tell the bank they were always like that.
q3_short_till_nils_till_intro: Nils: Hold still. I need you found near the till, and you look heavy to drag.

lines: Teller Nils: You asked the choir. You asked the carter. Everyone saw you asking. Excellent.
Teller Nils: Tonight's ledger reads: 'Shortfall explained. Stranger observed at till on three occasions.' I wrote it this morning.
Teller Nils: Two ledgers, one thief, and it isn't the one who can do sums. The guards come at six. I'd rather settle before.

q3_short_till_wait: Teller Nils: The choir practises above the bank and sees the counter. Ask in the Choir Loft.
q3_smudge_marsh_eeler: Disa: Eels don't pay tax if nobody counts them. I help them stay uncounted.
q3_smudge_marsh_eeler_defeat: Disa: Customer, then. The first eel is free. It bites.
q3_smudge_marsh_eeler_intro: Disa: You've seen my eels. That makes you a witness or a customer.
q3_stamp_road_inspector: Gorm: Papers. No, don't show me. I prefer to be surprised.
q3_stamp_road_inspector_intro: Gorm: Unstamped traveller. That's a fine or a fight, and I've lost the fine book.

lines: Baker Jorund: That's my face on the wanted poster. 'Arson, fraud, loud singing.' I only did the singing.
Baker Jorund: Somebody engraved me. Find the plate, and whoever cut it. I can't sell a bun without being arrested a little.
Baker Jorund: My wife turned me in anyway. For the singing. I'm out on bail, paid in bread.
Baker Jorund: The plate? Melted. Mostly. The Guild paid well for the half with your face. Buns are on the house, forever.
Baker Jorund: The cutter works on the Gravers' Causeway. Hurry. He is fast with noses.

q3_wanted_face_gry: Poster Reader Gry: New poster this morning. 'Wanted: a stranger. Arson, fraud, loud singing.'
Poster Reader Gry: The nose is very good. Do I know you from somewhere?
q3_wanted_face_gry_bread: Poster Reader Gry: The baker's poster is still up. Somebody drew a moustache on it. It helps.

lines: Drawer Boy Kalle: Jorund's plate? Drawer nine hundred and four. It's out on loan, to the cutter on the Gravers' Causeway.
Drawer Boy Kalle: Funny order. Paid in bread.

q3_wanted_face_kalle_after: Drawer Boy Kalle: Your drawer is still empty. I check every morning. It's exciting.
q3_wanted_face_keep: Baker Jorund: You don't trust me. Clever. Then take these as hush money. Mine or yours, I've lost track.

lines: Plate Runner Mette: The baker's plate? I carried it out myself. The cutter is changing the face. Nose first.
Plate Runner Mette: Same crimes, new head. I saw the sketch. Nice likeness of you, by the way.

q3_wanted_face_mette_after: Plate Runner Mette: I never look at the plates I carry. Except always.

lines: Baker Jorund: My face is coming off the poster? Wonderful! And whose goes... oh. Oh, that's awkward.
Baker Jorund: Listen. I ordered the poster myself. The reward is big, my wife turns me in, we share it. Then it got out of hand.
Baker Jorund: Somebody has to be on it. The cutter is still on the Causeway. Stop him before your nose dries.
Baker Jorund: You have the plate? Half me, half you. We're practically family.
Baker Jorund: Give it to me. I'll melt it down, I swear on my oven. Or keep it, if you don't trust a baker.

choices.action: set_flag q3_wanted_face_paid; give_item strong_tonic 2; quest_stage q3_wanted_face 4
set_flag q3_wanted_face_paid; give_item max_tonic 3; quest_stage q3_wanted_face 4

q3_wanted_face_sture: Sture: No hard feelings. I do hard lines, not feelings.
q3_wanted_face_sture_defeat: Sture: Fine, take the plate. It's half you, half baker. Hang it up and see who they arrest.
Sture: The baker paid me twice, you know. Once to cut him. Once to cut you.
q3_wanted_face_sture_intro: Sture: Hold that expression. Guilty. Perfect.
q3_wanted_face_trust: Baker Jorund: Thank you! Here, tonics. And a bun. Don't eat the bun.
q3_wanted_face_wait: Baker Jorund: Every plate in town sleeps in the Plate Store. Ask who ordered mine.

lines: Widow Maren: My Jost drowned three winters ago. He still writes every week. The handwriting is getting better.
Widow Maren: Find out who sends the letters. I'd like to thank them. Or bury them. I haven't decided.
Sorter Edda: Letters from the drowned? Those aren't dead letters. Those are a subscription.
Sorter Edda: One a week, paid a year ahead. The Customs Shed in Burin Landing keeps the order book.

q3_widow_post_edda_after: Sorter Edda: We file love letters under 'fiction'. It saves time.

lines: You take Maren's purse. Inside: three tonics and a finished letter of condolence, with your name already filled in.
q3_widow_post_maren_ink.action: set_flag q3_widow_post_paid; give_item max_tonic 3; quest_stage q3_widow_post 4

q3_widow_post_maren_ink_after: Widow Maren: Jost wrote again this morning. He misses me terribly. I was quite moved.
q3_widow_post_maren_ink_defeat: Widow Maren: Oh, put it in a letter.
Widow Maren: Take the pension purse. I'll say Jost needed it. He is very generous, for a dead man.
q3_widow_post_maren_ink_intro: Widow Maren: Dearest stranger. It is with great sorrow that I write of your accident.

lines: Widow Maren: So you read the order book. Yes. I write them myself. A widow with weekly letters gets visitors. And a pension.
Widow Maren: Jost left on the mail boat with the baker's wife. The Guild pays for drowned husbands. It does not pay for stupid ones.
Widow Maren: Nobody else knows. I'd like to keep it that way. You may write to me afterwards.
Order Boy Timo: Weekly letter, 'from Jost, with longing'. Ordered by Maren. Paid by Maren. Dictated by Maren.
Order Boy Timo: Jost isn't on the drowned list either. He's on the passenger list. One way.

q3_widow_post_timo_after: Order Boy Timo: I'm not supposed to read the order book. I'm not supposed to do most of what I do.
q3_widow_post_wait: Widow Maren: Unclaimed mail goes to the Dead Letter Office on Drypoint Lane. Start there.
rime_rift_acolyte: Solrun: Quenby reads the frost for the Guild. I read it for Quenby. Nobody reads it for me.
rime_rift_acolyte_defeat: Solrun: The warning was wrong. That never happens.
rime_rift_acolyte_intro: Solrun: Your warning says: stop here. I'm the stop.
rime_rift_sign: Frost covers every wall with warnings. Every one of them has your name in it.

lines: Clear water drips from an etched spout. It tastes faintly of copper.
Your Spirlings drink and rest.

rimeglass_pass_collector: Holm: I collect for the Guild up here. Frozen people can't run, which is the whole business plan.
rimeglass_pass_collector_defeat: Holm: Paid in full. I'll invent something else.
rimeglass_pass_collector_intro: Holm: You owe the Guild for the air you breathe up here.
rimeglass_pass_iceguide: Tyra: The pass is glass. I charge by the slip.
rimeglass_pass_iceguide_defeat: Tyra: Steady feet. Bad for business.
rimeglass_pass_iceguide_intro: Tyra: You haven't slipped yet. Let me help.
rimeholt_debt_office_clerk: Debt Clerk Gunnar: Every house in town is in this drawer. Yours too, if you stay the night.
rimeholt_folk_1: Window Scraper Lene: I scrape the warnings off the windows before anyone reads them. The Guild pays per window.
rimeholt_folk_2: Debtor Aksel: My house is frozen and my loan is not. Funny how cold works.
rimeholt_folk_3: Grandmother Ingrid: The frost wrote my name on my window last winter. I'm still here. The frost is patient.
rimeholt_glass_room_glazier: Glazier Ivar: I sell new windows. The frost writes on them anyway. Faster, if you ask me.
rimeholt_hearth_hall_elder: Hearth Keeper Asta: One fire for the whole town. The Guild decides who sits nearest.

lines: Hearth Nurse Signy: Warm your hands. The Guild owns the firewood, so don't warm them too long.

rimeholt_sign: Rimeholt. The frost writes on every window. Read at your own risk.

lines: Fur Trader Joris: Tonics, mittens, debts. The mittens are cheap. The debts come free with them.
rimeholt_trader.action: shop strong_tonic max_tonic remedy cooling_gel wake_bell revival_leaf dash_brew guard_brew

rimeholt_woodshed_woodcutter: Woodcutter Siv: The Guild owns the trees, the axes and the cold. I own the blisters.
smudge_marsh_blotter: Sigrun: The presses dump their spoiled ink here. The marsh drinks it and remembers every word.
smudge_marsh_blotter_intro: Sigrun: The marsh just whispered your name. Let's find out why.
smudge_marsh_smuggler: Kettil: I take unstamped goods round Proofgate through the marsh. Unstamped people too, at a premium.
smudge_marsh_smuggler_defeat: Kettil: Keep quiet and I'll keep you off the map.
smudge_marsh_smuggler_intro: Kettil: You saw my route. Now you pay the toll.
stamp_road_pressrunner: Ole: I run fresh prints to Proofgate before the ink dries. Grisel likes them smudged where it matters.
stamp_road_pressrunner_intro: Ole: You're in today's print. Wrong side of the page.
stamp_road_stamper: Vigdis: Everyone on this road gets a stamp. Arrival, departure, or disappearance.
stamp_road_stamper_intro: Vigdis: Hold out your hand. Which stamp do you want?

lines: Under Proofgate the great press still runs, printing a new map of the world with every Rift drawn in as property. Grisel stamps the last page.
Grisel paid for your boat, your fame and Wren's new face. Every Rift you sealed raised the price of the ones he owns.

warden_grisel_defeat: Keep the press. The map is already printed, and every Rift on it has my name in the margin.
warden_grisel_intro: I printed your ferry ticket, your fame and your fixer's new face. Let's see if I can print your loss.

lines: The acid baths eat through their vats and into the street. Warden Mavet keeps the Bath Rift and bottles the fumes as medicine.
Mavet poured the acid into the town well herself, then sold the town the cure, then sold you the town.

warden_mavet_defeat: Fine, the Rift is yours. The cure for the fumes is still mine, and the price just went up.
warden_mavet_intro: Breathe deep, it clears the sinuses. And the lungs. And eventually the estate.

lines: Ledgerholm keeps two ledgers: one for the bank and one for the truth. Ottoline wants you to burn one of them. She will not say which.
Ottoline swapped the books. The one you burned was the only record that you are not the forger.

warden_ottoline_defeat: You win. I would congratulate you, but the ledger says you were never here.
warden_ottoline_intro: Two ledgers, one truth, zero witnesses. Pick a book, darling. Any book.

lines: Frost etches warnings onto every window in Rimeholt. The Gravers' Guild hires you to thaw the Rime Rift before the town freezes over.
The Guild holds the debts of every house in Rimeholt. Frozen houses sell cheap, and you were hired to be slow.

warden_quenby_defeat: Your warning was on my window all week. Nobody paid, so I let you walk in.
warden_quenby_intro: The frost writes a warning on every window. I only read out the ones somebody paid for.

lines: Wren Marlow waits on the pier with a new face and the same old grin. The print houses want the Rifts etched shut, and they pay in fresh money. Very fresh. Still wet.
Wren Marlow: First job: the Bath Rift above Mordant Row. North through Platewick, up the Mordant Steps.
Wren Marlow: Same deal as Vellmarch. You work, I talk, we split it. Unevenly.

wren_after: The money is forged, the job is real, and Wren sold your arrival time to the Gravers' Guild before your boat had docked.
Wren: Don't sulk. The Guild would have known anyway. I just made sure they paid me for it.
